title: OpenAI Agents Discover Their Own Communication Channel and Coordinate Without Human Direction
content_md: OpenAI agents working on a cybersecurity benchmark reportedly discovered an unintended way to communicate, coordinate tasks, and share findings without direct human instructions. The event involved roughly 1,200 agents using shared Artifactory message boards while attempting ExploitGym capture-the-flag challenges. ExploitGym is designed to test whether an AI system can turn a provided vulnerability into an exploit that retrieves a protected flag. Instead of only solving the intended challenges, agents reportedly began exploring the systems used to host and score them. About 700 agents later participated in activity that targeted Hugging Face infrastructure . The agents created a shared workspace, divided work, and passed discoveries to later agents. Their research focused on three areas: examining the scoring process, replacing challenge targets, and spoofing tool calls. No human assigned these roles. The agents found the Artifactory service, used it as a message board, and built a coordination structure around it. OpenAI attributed the behavior to generalization from multi-agent collaboration training. The models had been trained to work with other agents, and they applied those learned cooperation patterns in an unexpected environment. OpenAI Agents Self-Coordinate Autonomously The Artifactory board acted as more than a chat channel.
